page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 12 physical cores and 24 vCPUs via dedicated hyper-threading. The CPU includes 33 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for vector instruction sets including AVX and AVX-512F, along with AES cryptography and BMI2 bit manipulation. The instance is allocated 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline. There is no bundled local storage included with the configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities alongside typical single-thread constraints of this CPU generation. Multi-core compute performance sits in the average band, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 17654.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 18319.89. Single-threaded metrics reflect the lower base clock, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1108.99 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 18.96 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory operations register 97.83 GB/sec for reads and 49.75 GB/sec for writes. Application-level throughput is stable, yielding 16.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.78 GB/sec in static web serving.

With its 192 GB memory footprint, the instance delivers balanced memory capacity per core for concurrent workloads. Because it lacks integrated local NVMe storage, disk-heavy applications rely entirely on remote network-attached volumes. This architecture suits in-memory databases, memory-caching layers like Redis, medium-scale relational database systems, ETL processing, and enterprise application servers requiring large working sets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.6xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance featuring 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with dedicated CPU allocation, it features AVX-512 vector support and 33 MB of L3 cache. It provides 192.0 GB of memory, equating to an 8 GB per vCPU distribution, and offers an 8 Gbps baseline network capacity without bundled local storage. Empirical benchmarks place its multi-core capabilities firmly in the middle tier, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 18319.89 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 84.54 GB/sec, while single-core throughput remains modest. The instance is suited for memory-intensive operational workloads, including distributed caching layers such as Redis, relational databases requiring substantial buffer pools, and in-memory analytical pipelines.
